tickets.title: As an Advisor, I want to override prerequisites, so that students graduate on time.
tickets.description:
1. Pass if an authorized Advisor account can successfully bypass a prerequisite block when clicking the "Override Restriction" button.
2. Pass if the system instantly logs the Advisor's ID, Student's ID, course details, and a timestamp into the immutable audit database trail.

tickets.title: As a Student, I want to drag classes to a calendar, so I can plan visually.
tickets.description:
1. Pass if a user can click a course block from the catalog list, drag it, and cleanly drop it into an available calendar time slot.
2. Pass if dropping a course into an overlapping time slot instantly triggers a distinct red visual warning overlay on the conflicting items.

tickets.title: As a Student, I want 8 AM class alerts, so that I avoid oversleeping.
tickets.description:
1. Pass if the system detects an 08:00 AM start time during configuration and triggers an explicit modal dialogue reading: "Warning: This class starts at 8:00 AM."
2. Pass if the system allows the user to acknowledge the alert and explicitly choose to either keep or discard the selected course block.

tickets.title: As a Student, I want private schedules, so that my data is protected.
tickets.description:
1. Pass if a logged-in student can exclusively view and edit their own active roadmap interface.
2. Pass if any attempt to view another student's schedule by guessing or forcing direct URL structures returns an explicit 403 Forbidden error screen.

tickets.title: As a Student, I want live class status tags, so I don't add full classes.
tickets.description:
1. Pass if a course with zero open seats immediately updates to display a greyed-out "Class Full" badge within the UI catalog layout.
2. Pass if the system restricts final validation submission when a student tries to save a full course into their final term registration queue.

analysis.ambiguity1: The requirement "the app to warn me if I am choosing a class that starts at 8:00 AM" is too vague because it does not define the technical nature or behavior of the warning. It fails to specify whether the system should display a non-blocking visual alert, an email notification, or completely block the action, making it impossible to create an exact test case.
analysis.ambiguity2: The requirement to "link to the live database" to block full classes, while simultaneously allowing students to "plan 4 years ahead" when future class capacities are completely unknown, is ambiguous. It lacks clear logical boundaries on how the system should handle future semester timelines where active database entries do not yet exist.
analysis.conflictSolution:
Conflict: The Registrar requires the system to block students from adding full classes using live database checks, whereas the Head of Advising wants students to be able to map out a full 4-year plan when capacity states are unknown.

Resolution: Implement a dual-state system featuring a "Draft Roadmap" mode and an "Active Registration" mode. For long-term planning (years 2 to 4), the system allows students to freely add courses without capacity constraints. For the current active semester, the system connects directly to the live database, flags full classes with a clear visual indicator, and restricts official validation until open slots are chosen.
analysis.nfr1: Data isolation constraint ensuring under no circumstances can any student access, view, or query another student's academic schedule or roadmap.
analysis.nfr2: The system must automatically generate a secure, read-only audit log entry every time an advisor triggers a manual prerequisite override.
analysis.nfr3: The calendar interface must support a highly responsive, low-latency drag-and-drop mechanism for real-time schedule manipulation.
